summary.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR317 crore (ROA 2.2%, ROE 18.2%); FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0%.
summary.overview: Gross loans reached INR42,903 crore (+28.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ) and deposits INR48,129 crore (+25% YoY), with CASA up 37.8% YoY to INR12,930 crore. Net interest income was INR1,186 crore with NIM stable at 8.5%, and GNPA fell 10 bps to 2.17% with PCR at 85%. Management revised FY27 credit cost guidance to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets and raised ROA guidance to 1.8-2.0%, helped by deferred capacity-building spend (about INR250 crore planned for FY27, mostly from June onward) and lower opex (now about 6.4% of average assets).

segments.name: Micro banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Book INR21,371 crore (+16.8% YoY), disbursements INR4,581 crore (+16.4% YoY). Bucket X collection efficiency 99.68%; slippages annualised about 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4; provision coverage about 95%.

segments.name: Affordable housing and micro mortgages
segments.commentary: Combined gross book INR11,210 crore (+40.8% YoY). GNPA stable at 1.2% (affordable housing) and 0.6% (micro mortgages). Micro mortgage book about INR1,800 crore, yield about 19.5%, PAR rising from about 1.2% to 1.5%.

segments.name: Secured book
segments.commentary: Secured book INR21,638 crore (+42.7% YoY, +7.8% QoQ), now 50.4% of loans.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Book INR3,470 crore (+54% YoY); new book GNPA 0.5%; MSME PAR down 13 bps. Ticket sizes rising, with LAP at INR80-90 lakh and working capital at INR1.1-1.2 crore; disbursement yield expected around 10.5%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,020 crore (+248.6% YoY); Q1 disbursements INR467 crore (+183.9% YoY). Sourced from 455 branches (106 added in the quarter); origination LTV 75%, book LTV about 56%.

segments.name: Vehicle loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,036 crore (+85.1% YoY), GNPA 1.7%, served through 337 branches with a mid-premium and EV focus. New lines (gold, vehicle, agri) are 7% of the loan book and 9% of Q1 disbursements.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0% (from the earlier guidance), citing opex and credit cost.
FY27 credit cost guidance revised to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets (earlier basis: average gross loan book); credit cost was 0.9% in Q1.
FY27 opex expected at about 6.4% of average assets, lower than earlier plan, as capacity spend (about INR250 crore) is deferred to later quarters.
FY27 planned asset growth of 25% reaffirmed.
Target of 56% secured loan mix by March 2027 maintained.
Bulk deposit ratio to stay around 30%; no immediate further deposit rate hikes seen, with marginal cost-of-funds increase expected.
Opex to decline year-on-year in FY28 as investment intensity eases.

qa_highlights.question: Can yields be sustained in affordable housing and non-MFI segments, and is 2% ROA possible on a steady-state basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Affordable housing yield around 12.5% with ticket INR16-20 lakh and about 580-590 branches; some competitive pressure but yields maintained. Micro mortgage yields about 19.5%, and yields do not fall much at INR10-12 lakh tickets.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost of funds rise further, and is any more deposit rate hike needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Brajesh Cherian said no immediate upward revision is needed, only a marginal increase in cost of funds is expected, and this is built into the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance. IBPC, refinance and securitisation are available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity-building spend and does the guidance embed NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Bala Kamath said about INR250 crore planned, with little spent in Q1 and spend starting in June; the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance includes it. NIM guidance given at the start of the year is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the credit cost guidance cut and are there early warning signs in MFI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Goel said MFI bucket X collection efficiency is 99.7% and July trends are similar; Q1 MFI slippages annualised about 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4. Each 5-7 bps move in collections would only marginally change credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the micro mortgage PAR and LGD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PAR rose from about 1.2% to about 1.5%; GNPA from about 0.47% to about 0.55%. Management says 18 and 24 MOB vintages have not exceeded about 2.5% and the book is still maturing; bucket X collection is 99.7-99.75%.

qa_highlights.question: How will opex trend after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is 6.4% of average assets in FY27; Sadananda Kamath said FY28 investment will be lower and opex will improve year-on-year, with exact figures to follow.

capex_capacity: Capacity-building spend planned at about INR250 crore for FY27; per management, little was spent in Q1 and spending started in June (marketing, IT, branch openings), building up over coming quarters.

Branch network at 814 as of June 2026 after 38 new branches in Q1; plan to add 144 branches in FY27 (106 yet to open). Gold loan active branches to rise from about 430-440 to about 575 by end-FY27; gold disbursement exit rate targeted at INR230-250 crore a month by March 2027 (June exit about INR170-175 crore a month).

Affordable housing capacity built at about INR350-375 crore disbursement a month; micro mortgage disbursement about INR100 crore a month, expected to reach INR140-150 crore by March 2027. Incremental book mix tilts toward micro mortgages.
Opex guided at about 6.4% of average assets for FY27; management expects FY28 opex to decline year-on-year as investment intensity eases.

New products: Unsecured Fast Track loan ready to scale after pilot; pre-owned car loans piloted in Karnataka, to test in 2-3 geographies this year; mid-corporate lending started in Q1; purchase invoice discounting added to MSME suite; co-branded credit card in testing. HCV/LCV only after FY27.
demand_pricing: Gross loans INR42,903 crore (+28.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ); disbursements INR9,245 crore (+41.4% YoY). Secured book INR21,638 crore, 50.4% of loans.

Micro banking book INR21,371 crore (+16.8% YoY), disbursements INR4,581 crore (+16.4% YoY); 1.72 lakh new customers in Q1. Management says demand is rising across almost all states; Kerala deliberately not being grown.
Affordable housing and micro mortgages INR11,210 crore (+40.8% YoY). Micro mortgage book about INR1,800 crore at ~19.5% yield; affordable housing yield about 12.5%, ticket INR16-20 lakh.

MSME book INR3,470 crore (+54% YoY). LAP ticket moved from INR58-60 lakh to INR80-90 lakh; working capital from INR70-80 lakh to INR1.1-1.2 crore. Disbursement yield expected around 10.5% vs earlier 11-11.5%, and below book yield.
Gold loans INR1,020 crore (+248.6% YoY); Q1 disbursement INR467 crore; monthly disbursement averaged INR160-170 crore in Q1. Vehicle loans INR1,036 crore (+85.1% YoY).

Deposits INR48,129 crore (+25% YoY); CASA INR12,930 crore (+37.8% YoY). Bulk deposit ratio about 30%, retail TD now said to be cheaper than bulk TD. Rates raised in June on key buckets; no immediate further hike seen. FCNR(B) raised about INR60 crore in Q1.
Cost of funds 6.86%, continuing to fall. Management sees only marginal increase ahead; no further repricing benefit visible. NIM stable at 8.5%; FY27 NIM guidance unchanged per management.
Competition: management acknowledged competitive pressure in affordable housing and CASA mobilisation and pricing pressure across asset products, but says yields are being held.
risks_watch: Deposit competition and CASA mobilisation: management flagged tight liquidity and deposit pressure; cost of funds may tick up marginally despite no further repricing benefit.
Yield pressure as ticket sizes rise in MSME (disbursement yield about 10.5%, below book yield) and affordable housing faces competition.
Monsoon and kharif sowing: management flagged El Nino and kharif delays as a key H2 monitorable; credit cost guidance relies on stable MFI collections.
Micro mortgage PAR rising (about 1.2% to 1.5%); management expects a natural increase as the book matures, so this needs monitoring.
Execution risk on the INR250 crore capacity spend and the 144-branch plan, which must lift deposits to fund the 25% asset growth; FY27 ROA guidance of 1.8-2.0% relies on it.
key_quotes: Our strategy continues to remain centered on strengthening our liability franchise, building a diversified asset portfolio and maintaining prudent risk management practices to ensure profitability along with growth.
This deferred commencement of expenses, coupled with ongoing efficiency gains will result in full year opex to be lower than earlier planned and now would be around 6.4% of average assets.
We are pleased to note that our progress towards diversification of loan portfolio remains on track with more than half of the loan book being secured at 50.4% as of June '26.

We remain mindful of the prevailing funding rate environment and the continued competitive intensity in CASA mobilization, along with pricing pressures across key asset products and the resulting impact on margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, credit cost and the raised ROA guidance, citing MFI collection efficiency of 99.7%. More cautious on liabilities, where management said deposit pressure is present and rate moves are being watched; it declined to give vertical-level profitability or product ROA.
